doc.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Playing the same way in every group; Dick Hyman's loose approach
summary: Tate says he does not change his style and is hired for it; good players make things work.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I don’t know, I try never to play differently. I just try to play. And it either works or it doesn’t. I can temper my style to a certain degree. For example last night, I don’t know if you heard the Dick Hyman set, Dick said, “Look,” he came to us before we played, he said, “let’s take a different approach to this, just play this very loosely and let it go where it goes.” And there’s certainly the structure, you know, we’re playing within the tune. So we’ll go to a certain length but I don’t try and do things that I can’t do. So I’m usually called because of the way I play. I play a certain style and so I don’t really have to think about it they already know what they’re getting.
I mean there’s a fairly ambiguous direction anyway, let’s play this fairly loose?

Well yeah, but I was thinking the other day, it just amazes me, with really good players, how much really works. Monk made a record with Pee Wee Russell and Bernard Purdie is on a Louis Armstrong record. And I don’t see people trying to change their style, they just go do what they do and when I think about it it really is pretty amazing how much does work if they’re really fine players.
Yeah. I guess you just have to listen.
